newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Strike paralyses Ivory Coast shipyard.
newsitem.headline: Strike paralyses Ivory Coast shipyard.

text.p: A pay strike paralysed Ivory Coast's French-owned ship building and repair firm CARENA for a sixth successive day on Monday with some sources saying that the management had locked out strikers.
Offshore oil and gas prospectors said the strike, which began on Wednesday, could affect their operations.
"The company is paralysed," one CARENA management source told Reuters, adding that there had been a "total lock-out." Industry sources say the lock-out began on Friday.
CARENA serves the offshore oil and gas exploration sector.
The Ivorian ship builders and repairers union SYLICORENA is demanding pay in line with naval repair and construction trades instead of mechanical industry rates.
"It does affect our operations. We are contracting a single legged oil platform which is under construction in the yard," said one exploration firm manager.
Offshore development supply vessels belonging to other firms had also been trapped by the strike, he said.
One CARENA spokesman said 10 vessels had been waiting at the firm's quay before the strike began. Many had since gone to other ports but three had stayed.
"Management cannot reply to the demands of the strikers," one manager said, adding that only the joint union and management body CIPC had authority to settle such pay disputes.

"(The strikers) want a naval pay scale which does not exist," CARENA's administration and finance director Michel Raguier said last week. Wages paid by CARENA were in line with Ivorian collective agreements, he added.
CARENA, owned by 50 percent shareholding French firms Bollore and Ateliers des Chantiers du Havre, employs 340 staff, with another 260 on contractual terms, including 20 expatriates.
